newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -BTP vols prove popular at high strikes.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -BTP vols prove popular at high strikes.

text.p: Implied volatility levels on BTP options traded on LIFFE inched up on Friday in limited activity as the futures contract tested resistance levels not seen since early 1994, traders said.
"It's been a very quiet day. The only real activity I've seen has been in BTP December out-of-the money options," said a broker at a Japanese bank in London.
He said out-of-the money December options volatility at the 122.00 strike on December BTP futures was roughly unchanged at 6.0 percent compared with 6.0 to 6.04 percent on Thursday.
Brokers quoted at-the-money volatility at 6.40 to 6.70 percent for December from 6.40 percent at Thursday's close.
At 1320 GMT, the December BTP future was at 118.57 up 45 basis points on the day.
The contract touched 119.10 earlier in the session, just below 119.12 seen on January 23, 1994 and 119.15 reached on February 6, 1994.
The broker said volatility might go up a little if the futures broke through this area, as the market questioned the contract's ability to sustain these levels.
"But it won't really go up unless there is a massive reversal. If the contract pulls back we'll get a sharp spike in volatility," he said.
He said December 122.00 strike calls had been bid up ten ticks during the session with two European banks buying heavily.
By 1320 GMT, nearly 5,000 lots at that strike had been traded, according to LIFFE data.
Elsewhere in the market, a Japanese bank trader said there had also been some buying of upside calls in Bunds suggesting volatility levels would rise.
"Bunds volatilities are so low they can only go one way and that is up," he said.
